by_judge.judge: JBJ WILL SIT IN COURT HALL NO. 3 AT PRINCIPAL BENCH BENGALURU

narrative:
On August 6, 2026, the Karnataka High Court achieved an overall hearing rate of 45.6%, processing 1,167 of the 2,560 scheduled cases across 44 judges. This represents a noticeable improvement over recent judicial days, rising from 38.4% on August 5 (1,095 of 2,849 heard), 39.8% on August 4 (1,013 of 2,546 heard), and exceeding the 44.5% rate recorded on August 3 (1,103 of 2,478 heard).

Judicial throughput varied across court halls. Justice M. Nagaprasanna addressed significant volume in Court Hall 14, hearing 120 of 225 scheduled matters (53.3%) in his primary list. In Court Hall 19, Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty heard 110 of 274 listed cases (40.1%). Several benches maintained high conversion rates, including Justice R. Nataraj at 77.6% (45 of 58 heard) and Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar at 77.0% (57 of 74 heard). Conversely, Court Hall 39 under Justice Rajesh Rai K recorded lower clearance, hearing 9 of 81 scheduled cases (11.1%).

By hearing stage, Preliminary Hearings logged the highest conversion rate at 69.4% (154 of 222 heard), followed by Admission matters at 48.1% (210 of 437) and Orders at 46.6% (459 of 984). The Orders stage showed marked progress compared to 35.3% on August 5. Final Hearing matters remained the most congested procedural bottleneck, converting at 22.0% (121 of 549). Among primary case types, Writ Petitions (WP) constituted the largest category with 951 listings, achieving a 44.7% hearing rate—an increase from 34.8% the previous day. Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) and Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) converted at 50.7% and 45.6% respectively, while Contempt of Court Cases (CCC) reached a 68.0% clearance rate.
